lessons.title: Money in vs money out
lessons.keyIdea: Money in is cash you add. Money out is cash that leaves. The tool shows what you entered.
paragraphs: A budget starts with two piles. Money in is cash that lands in your accounts. Money out is cash that leaves. The gap is what you can give a job.
This app does not invent money in. You add it. If you skip a deposit, Ready to Assign will be wrong. If you add a spend twice, Ready to Assign will be wrong. Budget shows what you entered.
You do not need a perfect history to start. Enter what you know for this month. The point is to see in versus out in one place — not to guess a lifestyle number.

cta.label: Open Budget and add money in or out

lessons.title: Envelopes and Ready to Assign
lessons.keyIdea: Ready to Assign is money not yet given a job. The number is whatever Budget shows.
paragraphs: An envelope is a job for cash: rent, food, a debt payment. You move Ready to Assign into envelopes. Ready to Assign is the point. It is money not yet given a job.
The number is whatever Budget shows. This page will not invent one. If Ready to Assign is missing or zero, that is the truth for now.
Giving Ready to Assign a job is how you decide. Spending from an envelope comes later. First see Ready to Assign. Then move it. The tool is the source, not this lesson.

cta.label: Open Budget and find Ready to Assign

lessons.title: Close the month so Ready to Assign is real
lessons.keyIdea: Close month carries Ready to Assign forward. Skipping close can make next month look empty.
paragraphs: A month is not done until you close it. Close month carries Ready to Assign and envelope balances into the next month. That is how Ready to Assign becomes real, not a sticky note.
Closing does not start you at zero. It does not delete last month. If you skip close, next month can look empty even when last month still had Ready to Assign.
Close when the month is actually over and the register looks right. The button lives inside a budget plan. After you close, use what Budget shows — not a number from this page.

cta.label: Open a budget and use Close month

lessons.title: Debt minimums first
lessons.keyIdea: Required debt payments get an envelope before wants. Budget will not pick a debt plan for you.
paragraphs: If you have a debt payment you must make, give it an envelope before you fund wants. A minimum is the amount you agreed to pay so the account stays current.
This is not a ranking of which debt to attack extra. It is order: required payments get a job first. Extra toward debt is a later choice, once Ready to Assign still remains.
Budget will not pick a debt plan for you. Make an envelope with the name you use at the lender. Fund it from Ready to Assign. The tool shows what you assigned.

lessons.title: When Ready to Assign can fund investing
lessons.keyIdea: Investing waits until Ready to Assign has cash with no job. Ready to Assign is one-time cash, not × 12.
paragraphs: Investing is optional until Ready to Assign says you have cash with no job. If Ready to Assign is missing or zero, there is nothing here to send to Invest. The tool wins.
Ready to Assign is one-time cash for this month, not a yearly income. Do not multiply it by 12. If you want to invest, assign Ready to Assign to that job, then record it in the Invest book.
You can still learn Invest with an empty book. Funding it is a later step. This lesson does not invent Ready to Assign or a buy list.
